lead.event: Rupiah Hits Record Weakness at Rp18,206 per US Dollar
lead.headline: Rupiah hits record weakness at Rp18,206 per US dollar
lead.blurb: The rupiah weakened 0.65% this week from Rp18,089, while the JISDOR rate fell 0.49% to Rp18,218 per dollar. CORE Indonesia economist Yusuf Rendy Manilet cited a stronger US dollar, rising US Treasury yields, expectations of Fed tightening, domestic political uncertainty and negative MSCI-related sentiment as sources of pressure. Bank Indonesia supported the currency through market interventions and government bond purchases. Next week, markets will watch US labor data and Bank Indonesia’s Board of Governors meeting, with the rupiah projected to trade between Rp18,100 and Rp18,250 per dollar.

deals_control.event: Deli Indonesia increases its stake in SINI
deals_control.headline: SINI Deli Indonesia raises stake with Rp10.75 billion in purchases
deals_control.blurb: Deli Indonesia, SINI’s controlling shareholder, bought 1.25 million shares in 22 transactions on 10–11 November. It said the purchases were for investment and that it intends to maintain control. SINI gained 43.46% over the week to 13 November.

deals_control.event: HRME Transfers Hotel The Hermitage After Execution Auction Settlement
deals_control.headline: HRME faces transfer of Rp489.58 billion hotel after execution auction
deals_control.blurb: Menteng Heritage reached an amicable settlement with related parties, including Hotel Menteng Jakarta, which won the execution auction. Its Rp205.35 billion obligation to Bank Mandiri will be netted to zero, though HRME will bear losses from the asset transfer.

deals_control.event: KB Bank Completes 85% Divestment of KB Bukopin Finance
deals_control.headline: BBKP completes 85% divestment of KB Bukopin Finance for Rp340 billion
deals_control.blurb: The sale to JB Woori Capital concluded on 4 November. KB Bank retains 14.24% of the finance company under a three-year lock-up, and its assets and liabilities are no longer consolidated. Existing credit facilities will continue through November 2028.

capital_raising_buybacks.event: GMFI Plans Rights Issue of Up to Rp1.06 Trillion
capital_raising_buybacks.headline: GMFI plans rights issue of up to Rp1.06 trillion
capital_raising_buybacks.blurb: The offer covers up to 22.03 billion Series B shares with a nominal value of Rp19 each. Proceeds would fund business development, expansion and working capital, subject to shareholder approval at an extraordinary meeting on 19 November.

market_structure_policy.event: MSCI proposes reclassifying Indonesia as a Standalone Market
market_structure_policy.headline: MSCI proposes reclassifying Indonesia as Standalone Market, decision due June 2027
market_structure_policy.blurb: MSCI cited share-ownership transparency, alleged coordinated insider trading and weak regulatory enforcement. Public policy observer Hafiz Elfiansya Parawu said oversight should be judged by supervision outcomes and called for earlier detection of violations, stronger agency coordination and better investor protection.

market_structure_policy.event: FTSE Russell removes 14 Indonesian HSC stocks from its indexes
market_structure_policy.headline: FTSE Russell will remove 14 Indonesian HSC stocks from its indexes
market_structure_policy.blurb: The deletions are part of the December 2026 review and take effect at the opening of trading on 21 December, using market prices at the review. FTSE Russell said it will monitor affected stocks’ liquidity to ensure deletion prices can be replicated. The final December GEIS changes list is due from 7 December.

market_structure_policy.event: MSCI removes BRMS and BRPT from its November 2026 index review
market_structure_policy.headline: MSCI removes BRMS and BRPT from Indonesia Index, moves BRMS to Small Cap
market_structure_policy.blurb: The November review removes BRPT entirely from the MSCI Indonesia Index and moves BRMS to the MSCI Global Small Cap Index. Changes take effect on 1 December, after trading closes on 30 November. MSCI’s next review announcement is due on 8 February 2027, with changes effective on 1 March.

earnings_guidance.headline: ICBP reports 14.5% nine-month sales growth to Rp64.44 trillion
earnings_guidance.blurb: Indofood CBP's instant noodle segment remained its largest contributor, with sales up about 14% to Rp48.01 trillion and operating profit rising to Rp11.09 trillion from Rp10.4 trillion. BRI Danareksa Sekuritas said premiumization, led by Indomie and cup noodles such as Pop Mie, boosted growth.

earnings_guidance.event: NCKL Reports Nine-Month 2026 Results Amid Cost and Nickel Pressures
earnings_guidance.headline: NCKL reports nine-month 2026 net profit of Rp8.69 trillion
earnings_guidance.blurb: Trimegah Bangun Persada recorded revenue of Rp26.87 trillion, while gross profit fell about 9% as production costs and royalties rose. Global nickel oversupply adds pressure, and NCKL’s removal from the LQ45 and IDX80 takes effect on 18 November.

earnings_guidance.event: PGEO targets 12.5% free float by March 2027 and 15% in 2028
earnings_guidance.headline: PGEO targets 12.5% free float by March 2027 and 15% in 2028
earnings_guidance.blurb: Pertamina Geothermal Energy said the targets support its capital-market compliance and governance efforts. It also said it respects the IDX’s periodic evaluations of LQ45 and IDX80 constituents.

earnings_guidance.headline: TUGU reports 17.4% nine-month profit growth
earnings_guidance.blurb: Tugu Insurance posted Rp495.15 billion in net profit attributable to owners for January-September 2026. Consolidated underwriting results rose 17.2% to Rp602.04 billion, including Rp306.2 billion from Fire Insurance and Rp159.8 billion from Marine Cargo.
